messages:
maya: Hey — seeing intermittent TLS renegotiation failures from edge proxies in eu-west-1 starting ~03:40 UTC. Failure pattern: client requests reneg, proxy attempts new handshake, then KMS decrypt DENY for keystore leading to connection drop. No major traffic change otherwise. Anyone seeing related alerts?

srebot: [ALERT] tls.handshake.failures spike +125% (eu-west-1) 03:40-03:55 — https://grafana.internal/alerts/9823 :rotating_light:

oliver: Can you paste a sample log slice and the proxy version? Also is this isolated to Private vs Hosted routing?

maya: proxy version: build-2026.03.03-az1. Logs:```
2026-03-21T03:41:02Z proxy[edge-123] INFO tls: renegotiation requested by client (SNI=myapp.eu)
2026-03-21T03:41:02Z keystore[edge-123] WARN KMS decrypt failed: AccessDenied (arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111:key/xxxx)
2026-03-21T03:41:02Z proxy[edge-123] ERROR handshake failed: no certificate available (keystore error)
2026-03-21T03:41:03Z proxy[edge-123] INFO connection closed, client_ip=1.2.3.4
```

This is happening across multiple proxies in the region (6/12). Not seeing same spike in ap-southeast yet.

kevin: Does the keystore rotator have permission to call KMS:Decrypt for that key? We rotated rotator IAM last week, recall a scoped change.

paula: I pushed an RBAC tightening to the rotator role yesterday at 03:25 (removed broad kms:Decrypt on legacy role, switched to new key-specific principal). I rolled the change via infra-apply. I also reverted a tiny bit at 03:50 after noticing some alerts (revert PR: https://git.internal/r/infra/345). Not sure if the revert fully propagated before the failures started.

oliver: Important — if the role change reduced rights on the old key and proxies still reference the older key IDs (or intermediate certs), that would explain KMS denies. Can we confirm which key ARN the failing keystore attempted to use?

maya: Confirmed failures reference arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111:key/xxxx (the old key). Rotator logs show a backfill job using cached certs but tries to decrypt for additional validation.

kevin: Ok. Two probable vectors: 1) rotator RBAC change caused transient KMS denies during cert refresh, 2) certain clients trigger renegotiation which forces immediate keystore access (no cache path). Suggest we enable debug for mtls handshake on a small canary and run a keystore sync check across proxies.

sre-oncall: We did a rolling restart of edge proxies in eu-west-1 at 03:30 for a separate deploy. That might coincide with rotator trying to re-seed keystores. I'll attach the deploy window: 03:30-03:36.

paula: I just checked: the revert PR succeeded at 03:50 but the IAM role change requires instance profile re-association (some proxies still had old creds cached). I'll open a ticket to force a re-assume across the fleet.

oliver: Short-term mitigation ideas: 1) Enable keystore local fallback (serve cached cert for 5m if KMS denies) 2) Temporarily permit KMS:Decrypt for the legacy rotator role while we reconcile key refs 3) Add a handshake-rate limiter for renegotiation to avoid thundering rekeys. Thoughts?

maya: I'm +1 on cached-cert fallback for edge proxies — reduces client impact while we fix roles. I'll flip the flag on a single proxy and run a canary.

kevin: I will audit IAM change history and KMS key policies now and post findings. If policy change is root cause we should add a pre-deploy check to ensure no live resource references old key ids.

paula: I'll coordinate the forced re-assume / instance-profile refresh across eu-west-1 and post status here. Filing compliance audit ticket for RBAC change (link after creation).

oliver: Also add an observability metric: count of tls.renegotiation.requests that cause keystore hits vs cache hits. That will help evaluate the mitigation.

maya: Running keystore sync check on the 6 affected proxies now; will paste results.

srebot: [INFO] runbook suggestion: enable mtls debug, enable keystore fallback, escalate IAM rollback if more than 10% of proxies fail after re-assume.

maya: Quick canary result: cache fallback -> success, client connections continued with no further handshake failures on that proxy for 10m.

kevin: IAM audit: rotator role PR removed legacy KMS:Decrypt on the role used by older proxies. New role has correct key policy. Evidence: https://iam.internal/audit/rotator/7245. Recommend short-term widen to include the legacy key ARN until all proxies reattach.

paula: Opening ticket INFRA-7239 to force re-assume and record RBAC justification for SOC review. Assigning to infra-runbooks.

oliver: Next steps (owners): maya -> run full keystore sync and post list of proxies still referencing legacy key (due +15m); kevin -> update IAM policy recommendation and prepare emergency allowlist if needed (+10m); paula -> execute re-assume job and ticket creation (+20m).

maya: Ack, will post results. :eyes:

paula: Thanks — I'll also add an audit log entry with the RBAC change diff for compliance.

sre-oncall: I'll monitor Grafana and get an SLA blameless postmortem if the rollback window extends.

oliver: Great coordination, keep incremental status messages short.

maya: Posting results: 4 proxies still referencing legacy key (edge-101, edge-104, edge-109, edge-111). KMS denies correspond to those hosts.

kevin: Thx. Pushing emergency allow for legacy key for 30m to stop customer impact while re-assume finishes. Notifying compliance.

paula: Re-assume job in progress — starting now.

srebot: [RESOLVED] tls.handshake.failures returned to baseline in eu-west-1 at 04:02 UTC. Incident closed (auto-check).

maya: Confirming: after re-assume + temp allow, handshakes normal. Will follow up with a short playbook writeup and a pre-deploy key-ref check.

oliver: Please convert this thread into a short runbook entry and link to INFRA-7239. Good catch everyone. :thumbsup:
